course.title: AWS — From Cloud Fundamentals to Professional Architecture
course.description: A visual-first AWS learning path from cloud/account foundations through IAM, networking, compute, storage, databases, serverless, containers, security, automation, reliability, analytics, AI, migration and Well-Architected design. All content remains draft until technical review.
course.version_scope: AWS documentation checked for core concepts and selected current product facts on 2026-10-11. Service availability, console workflow, pricing, quotas, feature packaging and certification objectives must be rechecked immediately before publication. CLI examples are read-only where executable; YAML/JSON/code samples are static instructional fragments unless stated otherwise.
prerequisites: No previous AWS experience is required. Basic computer literacy is enough to begin; networking, command-line and application/database concepts are introduced when needed. Hands-on cloud work requires an account owner-approved sandbox and spending controls.
learning_outcomes: Explain cloud computing and select suitable AWS service categories for common workloads.
Design and review account boundaries, IAM permissions, network paths, compute, storage and database access.
Plan application, serverless and container architectures with monitoring, delivery, recovery and cost controls.
Use approved read-only AWS CLI/SDK workflows and reason about IaC, CI/CD and operational signals.
Evaluate workload decisions against the six AWS Well-Architected pillars and document evidence-based trade-offs.

source_pdf.source_note: The PDF overview and final note claim 287 lesson identifiers, but the complete enumerated Section B lists a continuous 1–285 sequence (285 topics). This course preserves all 285 visible topic IDs and does not invent 286–287.
